_meta.indication: Treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in pediatric patients 6 to 17 years of age

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, three-arm placebo-controlled, parallel-group monotherapy trial; 6-week treatment (1-week titration, 5-week maintenance)
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients 6 to 11 years of age with ADHD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to end of study in ADHD Rating Scale-5 (ADHD-RS-5) total score
pivotal_trials.n: N=477 randomized (placebo N=155, 100 mg N=147, 200 mg N=158)
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses superior to placebo in ADHD-RS-5 change from baseline: 100 mg LS mean difference -4.2 (95% CI -6.5, -1.9), p=0.0003; 200 mg LS mean difference -4.3 (95% CI -6.6, -2.1), p=0.0002

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, three-arm, placebo-controlled, parallel-group monotherapy trial; 8-week treatment (3-week titration, 5-week maintenance)
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric patients 6 to 11 years of age with ADHD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to end of study in ADHD Rating Scale-5 (ADHD-RS-5) total score
pivotal_trials.n: N=313 randomized (placebo n=97, 200 mg n=107, 400 mg n=97)
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses superior to placebo in ADHD-RS-5 change from baseline: 200 mg placebo-subtracted difference -6.0 (95% CI -10.0, -1.9); 400 mg placebo-subtracted difference -5.8 (95% CI -9.9, -1.7)

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, three-arm, placebo-controlled, parallel-group monotherapy trial; 6-week treatment (1-week titration, 5-week maintenance)
pivotal_trials.population: Pediatric (adolescent) patients 12 to 17 years of age with ADHD
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to end of study in ADHD Rating Scale-5 (ADHD-RS-5) total score
pivotal_trials.n: N=310 randomized (placebo n=104, 200 mg n=94, 400 mg n=103)
pivotal_trials.result: Both doses superior to placebo in ADHD-RS-5 change from baseline in adolescents: 200 mg placebo-subtracted difference -4.5 (95% CI -8.4, -0.6); 400 mg placebo-subtracted difference -5.1 (95% CI -8.9, -1.3)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and at least twice the placebo rate): somnolence, decreased appetite, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, and irritability. Somnolence occurred in 16% of Qelbree-treated vs 4% of placebo patients; fatigue 6% vs 2%.
target_moa: Viloxazine is a norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor; it binds the norepinephrine transporter (NET) and inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine, increasing noradrenergic neurotransmission

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SUICIDAL THOUGHTS AND BEHAVIORS — higher rates of suicidal thoughts and behavior were reported in pediatric patients treated with Qelbree than with placebo; closely monitor for worsening and emergence of suicidal thoughts and behaviors

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication and there were no controversial issues

description.text: Expanded indication to include treatment of ADHD in adults

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes the addition of safety and efficacy data for the use of Qelbree (viloxazine extended-release capsules) for the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults. Qelbree is now indicated for the treatment of ADHD in adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older.

summary.text: Standard 505(b)(1) NDA for viloxazine ER (Qelbree) for pediatric ADHD; the original application received a Complete Response letter on November 6, 2020 for manufacturing facility deficiencies, and was approved following a Class I resubmission received February 3, 2021.
